about: The import table of proposals/wasm-runtime.md: every import a runtime "wasm" cart may declare, all from module "moy". params and results are wasm value types; wamr is the WAMR NativeSymbol signature string for the same function; spec is the SPEC.md section whose verb this is, or "wasm" for the binding's own. Tracks the proposal: not part of core 0.3.

imports.name: cls
imports.notes: cls(c). Lua's default c is 0.

imports.name: background
imports.notes: background(c).

imports.name: view
imports.notes: view(w, h). Lua's defaults are W and H.

imports.name: pix
imports.notes: pix(x, y, c). c >= 0 writes and returns 0; c < 0 is Lua's two-argument form and returns the index at x, y (0 off the canvas).

imports.name: line
imports.notes: line(x0, y0, x1, y1, c).

imports.name: rect
imports.notes: rect(x, y, w, h, c), filled.

imports.name: rectb
imports.notes: rectb(x, y, w, h, c), outline.

imports.name: circ
imports.notes: circ(cx, cy, r, c), filled.

imports.name: circb
imports.notes: circb(cx, cy, r, c), outline.

imports.name: oval
imports.notes: oval(x, y, w, h, c), filled.

imports.name: ovalb
imports.notes: ovalb(x, y, w, h, c), outline.

imports.name: print
imports.notes: print(s, len, x, y, c). s is len bytes of linear memory, walked one byte per cell; a compiled cart formats its own numbers.

imports.name: camera
imports.notes: camera(x, y, out). camera() is camera(0, 0). The previous offset, Lua's two results, is written at out as two i32 unless out is 0.

imports.name: clip
imports.notes: clip(x, y, w, h). clip() is clip(0, 0, W, H).

imports.name: pal
imports.notes: pal(c0, c1, p). p = 1 is the screen palette, as in Lua; c0 < 0 is pal() and resets both palettes.

imports.name: palt
imports.notes: palt(c, on). c < 0 is palt() and resets.

imports.name: fillp
imports.notes: fillp(p, c). fillp() is fillp(0, -1); c < 0 leaves holes untouched.

imports.name: make_layer
imports.notes: make_layer(w, h). A layer handle, or 0 where Lua returns nil (the host declined). Lua's defaults are W and H. A layer lives until the cart ends.

imports.name: draw_layer
imports.notes: draw_layer(layer, cx, cy). layer is a handle make_layer returned; any other value traps.

imports.name: tri
imports.notes: tri(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, c), filled.

imports.name: trib
imports.notes: trib(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, c), outline.

imports.name: tline
imports.notes: tline(x0, y0, x1, y1, u, v, du, dv, colorkey). u, v, du, dv are 16.16 fixed point; Lua's default colorkey is -1.

imports.name: spr
imports.notes: spr(n, x, y, colorkey, scale, flip). Lua's defaults: colorkey -1, scale 1, flip 0.

imports.name: sspr
imports.notes: sspr(sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy, dw, dh, colorkey, flip). Lua's defaults: dw = sw, dh = sh, colorkey -1, flip 0.

imports.name: sget
imports.notes: sget(x, y).

imports.name: sset
imports.notes: sset(x, y, c).

imports.name: fget
imports.notes: fget(n, b). b < 0 is Lua's fget(n) and returns the flag byte; otherwise 1 or 0 for bit b.

imports.name: fset
imports.notes: fset(n, b, v). b < 0 is Lua's fset(n, v) and writes v as the byte; otherwise bit b is set when v is non-zero and cleared when it is 0.

imports.name: map
imports.notes: map(mx, my, w, h, sx, sy, colorkey, scale, layers). Lua's w and h default to the map's edge, which a compiled cart passes itself; colorkey -1, scale 1, layers 0.

imports.name: mget
imports.notes: mget(x, y). -1 for an empty cell or out of range.

imports.name: mset
imports.notes: mset(x, y, tile).

imports.name: btn
imports.notes: btn(b, player). b indexes SPEC.md 7.3's buttons in its order -- left 0, right 1, up 2, down 3, a 4, b 5, run 6 -- where Lua passes the name; any other index reads 0. Returns 1 or 0.

imports.name: btnp
imports.notes: btnp(b, player). b as for btn. Returns 1 or 0.

imports.name: players
imports.notes: players(). Always at least 1.

imports.name: touch
imports.notes: touch(out). 0 where Lua returns nil (no pointer); otherwise 1, with x, y, tapped, held written at out as four i32 unless out is 0.

imports.name: key
imports.notes: key(code). code < 0 is key() and returns the last typed code, 0 for none; otherwise 1 or 0.

imports.name: keyp
imports.notes: keyp(code). code < 0 is keyp() and returns the last typed code, 0 for none; otherwise 1 or 0.

imports.name: textmode
imports.notes: textmode(on).

imports.name: sfx
imports.notes: sfx(n, chan). Lua's default chan is -1: round-robin.

imports.name: music
imports.notes: music(track, loop). Lua's default loop is 1.

imports.name: music_stop
imports.notes: music_stop().

imports.name: sound_stop
imports.notes: sound_stop(chan). chan < 0 stops every channel, which is Lua's sound_stop().

imports.name: volume
imports.notes: volume(level).

imports.name: beep
imports.notes: beep(freq, dur). Lua's default dur is 0.15.

imports.name: time
imports.notes: time(). Milliseconds since the cart started: the binding's only clock.

imports.name: pmem
imports.notes: pmem(slot, v, write). write 0 is Lua's pmem(slot): returns the slot, v ignored. write 1 is pmem(slot, v): stores v and returns 0.

imports.name: cfg
imports.notes: cfg(key, key_len, dst, dst_len). Copies the value's text -- a string without its quotes, a number as config.json spells it -- into dst, at most dst_len bytes, and returns its whole length; -1 where Lua returns the caller's default. Applying a default and parsing a number are the cart's.

imports.name: rnd
imports.notes: rnd(n). Lua's default n is 1.0.

imports.name: srand
imports.notes: srand(seed).

imports.name: flr
imports.notes: flr(x).

imports.name: quit
imports.notes: quit(). Does not return: the host unwinds the cart and ends it as the cart's own choice, not as a trap.

imports.name: target
imports.notes: target(layer). The drawing verbs a Lua layer answers as methods (cls pix line rect rectb circ circb oval ovalb print camera clip pal palt fillp spr map tri trib sspr tline) draw into layer from here on; 0 is the screen. Lua's ly:rect(...) is target(ly) rect(...) target(0). The target is the screen whenever the host calls an export; a handle make_layer never returned traps.

imports.name: blit
imports.notes: blit(frame, pal). frame is W x H bytes of indices, row-major; pal is 0 for the cart's own palette (SPEC.md 2.2, index taken modulo 64) or 768 bytes of RGB, a 256-entry palette for this frame. Writes the whole screen, ignoring camera, clip, both palettes, palt, fillp and the target. Only inside _draw, and at most one blit or blit565 per _draw; anything else traps.

imports.name: blit565
imports.notes: blit565(frame). frame is W x H RGB565 words, little-endian, row-major. Otherwise exactly blit's rules.

imports.name: read
imports.notes: read(name, name_len, offset, dst, len). Copies up to len bytes of the cart's own file name, from byte offset, into dst and returns how many it copied. With len 0 it copies nothing and returns how many bytes remain from offset. An absent name, a name outside the cart's folder, or an offset past the end reads 0.

imports.name: snd
imports.notes: snd(pcm, n). pcm is n frames of signed 16-bit mono, little-endian, at 22050 Hz. Queues as many as the host has room for and returns how many; with n 0 it reads nothing and returns the room. The host holds at most 2048 frames its output has not yet taken, and a host with no audio drains them at the rate and drops them. A range outside linear memory traps.

imports.name: par
imports.notes: par(n, arg, stacks, size). Runs the cart's _par(i, arg) export for every i in [0, n), across the host's cores or one after another on one, and returns when all have. Item i runs with the cart's __stack_pointer at stacks + (i + 1) * size, which the host puts back after. stacks and size are multiples of 16 and the n * size bytes from stacks lie in linear memory, or it traps. An item calls no import (one that does traps) and writes nothing another item reads or writes. A trap in an item traps par with the lowest trapping item's message.
